Caterine had $(10\,\frac{3}{4}-9\,\frac{2}{7})$ liters of distilled water left over.
 
Writing $10\,\frac{3}{4}$ as an improper fraction, we have

$$
10\,\frac{3}{4}=\frac{10\times 4+3}{4}=\frac{43}{4}.
$$

Writing $9\,\frac{2}{7}$ as an improper fraction, we have

$$
9\,\frac{2}{7}=\frac{9\times 7+2}{7}=\frac{65}{7}.
$$

Therefore, our problem now is to work out the following:

$$
\frac{43}{4}-\frac{65}{7}
$$

To subtract two fractions with unlike denominators, we need to express each fraction as an equivalent fraction with a common denominator.

In this question, we can make a common denominator of $28.$

To put $\frac{43}{4}$ over a denominator of $28,$ we multiply the numerator and denominator by $7:$

$$
\frac{43}{4}=\frac{43\times 7}{4\times 7}=\frac{301}{28}
$$

To put $\frac{65}{7}$ over a denominator of $28,$ we multiply the numerator and denominator by $4:$

$$
\frac{65}{7}=\frac{65\times 4}{7\times 4}=\frac{260}{28}
$$

We can now subtract the fractions. We keep the denominator the same, and we subtract the numerators:

$$
\frac{301}{28}-\frac{260}{28}=\frac{41}{28}
$$

Finally, we convert back to a mixed number:

$$
\frac{41}{28}=1\,\text{R}\,13=1\,\frac{13}{28}
$$

Therefore, the volume of distilled water remaining equals $1\,\frac{13}{28}$ liters.
